We have seen multiple reports about Apple Vision Pro applications in medical settings. This week, Stryker announced the completion of the first surgical procedure using an innovative Vision Pro application.

The procedure was a hip arthroscopy, performed using the SportSuite Vision application, which can bring "critical digital content into the surgeon's virtual space." The content includes arthroscopic imaging, HipCheck, HipMap, and CT scan images.

Below is Stryker's description of the application:

SportSuite Vision brings critical digital content into the surgeon's visual space, enabling them to simultaneously view physical objects and digital tools within the operating room, such as arthroscopic imaging, HipCheck, HipMap, and CT scan images. During arthroscopic procedures, surgeons typically need to rely on multiple displays in the operating room to access imaging and surgical data. By integrating multiple data sources into the surgeon's field of view, this technology can reduce reliance on traditional displays and support a smoother, more ergonomic surgical workflow.

SportSuite Vision received De Novo authorization from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on July 17. Stryker stated that this is the first application to receive FDA authorization for use with Vision Pro during surgery.
